properties.project_name: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
properties.digitized_from: Outlined as the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (one piece of 19,181.78 sqm before cutting). Pier & Point split that piece in three at its two natural narrow points (lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then combined parts by hand: P23 is the north part (the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (the plaza) that lies east of the line where the lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south. Not taken from a surveyed parcel.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20: the owner corrected the prior resolution (which had P23 'landing exactly inside the already-tracked real footprint of Chase Center, not a separate undeveloped parcel'). Re-derived via the numbered real-gap-fragment technique: fragment 2 (19,181.78 sqm) was first split into 3 pieces at real cross-sectional width-scan waists (piece0 south lawn, piece1 middle plaza, piece2 north lawn -- same nseg/width-minimum method used for P26). The owner then specified P23's exact construction: take piece2, cut off its 'panhandle' (the ~850 sqm sliver hugging the Vision Center building's stepped roofline, cut at the point (lon -122.386948, lat 37.766912) where piece2's cross-section narrows from the open lawn into that sliver), keeping only the wide main lawn body (2,283 sqm); then extend that same narrowing seam (a vertical cut at lon -122.386948) south through piece1, and add the portion of piece1 east of it (4,497 sqm, the open tree-lined plaza around the pavilion, as opposed to the ~4,087 sqm west portion that hugs both buildings and the pavilion itself, which stays unassigned). Result: 6,780 sqm, a continuous landscaped plaza/lawn from the Chase Center roundabout down to the pavilion. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: source_doc_urls was empty and now lists the OCII Dec 2019 Land Use Map (places P23 at 16th St / Terry Francois east of X4, park-green), the OCII Sept 2023 transition presentation (the Port will manage P23) and SocketSite's April 2019 article (P23/P24 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'). The Vision Center / Chase roundabout description in the notes remains this repository's own observation. The pavilion beside this plaza is not the Mission Creek Park Pavilion (290 Channel St, about 800 m north-west). 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, digitized_from reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery and the street/already-tracked-polygon-bounded gap computation, divided at owner-specified cross-sectional seams rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23 & P24'); SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left untracked as its own P-number pending further review.'; digitized_from: 'Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (fragment 2, 19,181.78 sqm raw). The owner reviewed a 3-way width-scan split of that fragment (at its two real cross-sectional waists, lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then gave a precise construction: P23 is the north piece (piece2, the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (piece1, the plaza) that lies east of the seam where piece2's lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery, outlined as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes and divided at seams chosen by hand by Pier & Point, rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23 & P24'); SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left off the map, pending further review of whether it is a separate plan parcel.
properties.notes: OCII plan open-space parcel P23. Landscaped lawn and plaza between the Chase Center roundabout and the pavilion, east of the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision.
